text: Today, we are going to make a quick and easy paneer akuri recipe with very few ingredients. It's quick to make but tastes equally delicious and flavorful. Let's get started without wasting any time. Turn on the gas. We need to add oil to it. After the oil is hot, we need to add four finely chopped green chilies to the tempering. Add ginger-garlic paste.

So, we'll add a small spoon of onion, two medium onions, finely chopped, to it. We need to sauté it well, a little on the reddish side. We'll add salt to this onion, a little, so that the onion also softens and cooks quickly. Again, we need to sauté it well. Once it turns a little reddish, we'll add all the spices to it.

Let's add the spices. Add half a teaspoon of turmeric powder and one teaspoon of coriander powder. We have taken about one to one and a half teaspoons of red chili powder. If you have Sambhar Masala, you can use that too. If not, you can use Sambhar Masala. I have added one and a half teaspoons of Sambhar Masala. Mix it well.

Once it's mixed, we need to add tomatoes to it immediately. I've taken three tomatoes here, finely chopped. After sautéing them well, we need to add finely chopped coriander leaves to it. Let's add a little water and mix well. Turn the heat down a bit and let it cook nicely.

So far, what we need to do is take 250 grams of paneer and put it in this large bowl, and then mash it up nicely with your hands. Do you know the fun thing? When we say "Akuri," we immediately know that it's a Parsi dish. The only difference is that we are making this paneer Akuri. And as I said, you can use Dhansak masala. This is a special Parsi spice, so you should only use it if you have it.

It's fantastic! Now, it's all mixed together nicely. Once the tomatoes are a little mushy, you can see what we need to do. It's also releasing a good amount of oil. We need to add the crumbled paneer to it. Mix it all together nicely.

Let's add a little water and stir it well. We have taken a little water because we don't want to dry it out; we want to keep it a little moist. This is called paneer vegetable, it's also called Akuri. Let's turn off the gas. The vegetable is ready, and let's finish it off well. Sprinkle some coriander leaves, and that's it.
So, paneer akuri is ready, folks! This is a Parsi dish that is quick and delicious. Do try it, and don't forget to let us know after you've made it. See you next time in the next episode.
